name: Say It Right
description: Why taxonomy comes before pipeline: the boundaries of a CDP-shaped system, the tracking plan as reviewed, tested code, the versioning rules that decide whether your analytics history survives the next release, and the contracts compiled from the plan — including what a good rejection reason is worth at 3am. Covers RFCs 0001 and 0002.

steps.title: Orientation and prerequisites
steps.validates: Can you state in one sentence what this repository is for, and do the prerequisite tools run on your machine?

verify.name: Event gateway readiness endpoint answers (keep the app running in another terminal)

steps.title: Boundaries: why collection, identity, analytics, and activation are separate
steps.validates: Why must the gateway accept an event even when identity resolution, the warehouse, and every destination are down — and what does that force to be true about the event stream?

verify.name: Unit tests and tracking-plan checks pass

steps.title: The tracking plan, and breaking it on purpose
steps.validates: Which changes to an existing event are safe within version 1, and which force a version 2 — and why does renaming a property in a shipped client cost more than it appears to?

verify.name: Tracking plan parses and satisfies the conventions
Working tree is clean again after the break-it exercise

steps.title: Contracts compiled from the plan, and rejections worth reading
steps.validates: Why is validation compiled from the tracking plan rather than written per event, why does each rejection carry a specific reason instead of "invalid", and why is the gateway live but not ready when the plan will not compile?

verify.name: Contract tests pass, including the generated-types drift check
A planned event is accepted by the CLI
A browser-sent money event is refused for the right reason
The gateway publishes the contract catalogue (keep the app running in another terminal)
Working tree is clean again after the break-it exercises
